MelonUI

MelonUI is a C# library for building console user interfaces. You can create pages and controls in C#, or use MXML, an XML-based markup language, to describe the UI in a file.

About

The library is built around UIElement, the base class used by each control. ConsoleWindowManager handles displaying the UI and processing input, while your application provides the data and the methods called by the controls.

C# and MXML use the same controls and element tree, so you can choose the approach that works best for your application. You can also load an MXML page and access its elements from C#.

Features

  • Built-in Controls: Text input, menus, buttons, progress bars, color pickers, and layout containers are included.
  • MXML: Pages can be written in markup and recompiled while the application is running. If an edit fails to compile, the previous page is kept.
  • Data Binding: Controls can read and update properties on your application objects, and call methods when the user interacts with them.
  • Custom Controls: You can derive from UIElement and use the binding generator to add your own properties.
  • Keyboard Controls: The window handles focus navigation, while individual controls handle editing and selection.

Guides

There are guides on how the different parts of MelonUI work and how to use them:

  • Layout and Styling
    • How to position elements, divide a page into cells, and change its colors.
  • Managing Elements
    • How to add, remove, reuse and dispose controls.
  • ConsoleWindowManager

  • Focus and Keyboard Controls

  • Popups and Dialogs

  • MXML Guide
    • How to write, load and update markup pages.
  • Data Binding

Developing Custom Controls

If the built-in controls do not cover what you need, you can create a class that derives from UIElement. See the Custom Controls Guide for a complete example, and the Binding Generator documentation for adding bindable properties.

Reference Documentation

The Controls Overview lists the built-in elements with C# and MXML examples. The API Reference also includes the supporting types, such as MenuItem, WorkItem and the binding classes.

MelonUI targets .NET 10. The optional MelonUI.Shaders library contains the GPU controls; it is not needed for a normal console UI. Build instructions and platform information are in Building MelonUI.
